<a id="tool-get_asset_preview"></a>
## `get_asset_preview` — Get Asset Preview

Get inline image previews for digital assets so the user can see them. Use when the user wants to SEE / VIEW / DISPLAY / RENDER specific assets or images. Accepts a list of asset IDs — typically obtained from query_asset (or any other tool that returns asset IDs). Returns a JSON object with a `previews` array of { assetId, url } — render each as !\[assetId](url) in your reply so the user can see the images. URLs are short-lived presigned links. Do NOT use for searching, listing, or counting assets — use query_asset for that.

- **CF module:** Assets
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `assetIds` | JsonElement? | no | Asset IDs to fetch preview images for. Pass as a JSON array of strings, e.g. ["id1","id2"]. Get IDs from query_asset or any tool that returns assetIds. |

**Example input**

```json
{ "assetIds": ["a1b2c3", "d4e5f6"] }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "previews": [ { "assetId": "a1b2c3", "url": "https://cdn.../a1b2c3.jpg?sig=...", "fileName": "shot_001.jpg" } ], "missing": [], "truncated": false }
```

**Known limitations**

Hard cap of 200 asset IDs per call (extras are dropped and `truncated: true` is returned). Preview URLs are short-lived presigned links that expire. Returns images only — use query_asset to search/list/count.

<a id="tool-get_talent_crew_preview"></a>
## `get_talent_crew_preview` — Get Talent & Crew Preview

Inline avatar GALLERY widget for a list of talent crew IDs. **TRIGGER STRICTLY when user prompt is purely visual** — e.g. 'show me their faces', 'what do they look like', 'photo gallery of these models'. **DO NOT TRIGGER**:   • after `query_talent_crew` (its table widget already shows Photo column)   • after `query_talent_crew_schedule` (its widget renders avatars inline post-improvements-v1)   • for 'show profile' / 'who is X' / 'list talents' (use `query_talent_crew`) **Best fit**: standalone visual question without data context. Returns `previews` array of { talentCrewId, displayName, avatarUrl, deepLinkUrl }. Widget owns visual — text response = ONE sentence ('Showing N avatars.').

- **CF module:** Talent & Crew
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `talentCrewIds` | JsonElement? | no | Talent crew IDs to fetch avatar previews for. Pass as a JSON array of strings, e.g. ["id1","id2"]. |

**Example input**

```json
{ "talentCrewIds": ["t-101", "t-102"] }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "previews": [ { "talentCrewId": "t-101", "name": "Jane Doe", "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.../t-101.jpg?sig=..." } ], "missing": [] }
```

**Known limitations**

Visual-only avatar gallery. Do NOT chain after query_talent_crew or query_talent_crew_schedule — those already render avatars. Avatars are resolved in chunks of 50; talent without an avatarId are omitted.

<a id="tool-query_asset"></a>
## `query_asset` — Query Asset

List or count/aggregate digital asset metadata (id, name, step, dates) — does NOT return preview images. Use when the user wants to FIND, LIST, or COUNT assets/photos/shots/deliverables. Filter by job, product, production type, step, workspace, photographer, stylist, model, star rating, time range. Drill-down: pass workUnitIds/jobIds/productIds from upstream queries. When groupBy params set, returns counts/aggregations instead of list. Default: latest step only when step not specified. Use names for filters (production type, step). IDs accepted as fallback. If the user wants to SEE/VIEW/RENDER the images, follow up with the get_asset_preview tool using the returned asset IDs.

<a id="tool-query_ecomm_production"></a>
## `query_ecomm_production` — Query E-Comm Production

Search productions (work units) — the central entity tracking a product through the workflow. Use this to answer: what step is a production on, who's working on it, how many are done/in-progress, production counts by photographer/vendor/location/type, and turnaround times. Status: New, Todo, InProgress, Done. Step names: Photography, InternalPostProduction, FinalSelection, etc. Filter by job, product, sample, production type, vendor team, post-production vendor, photographer, stylist, model, art director, videographer, digital-processing user, location, workspace. **Job lookup param choice — strict per user phrasing:** caller says 'job code JOB-123' → `jobCode`; 'job named Spring Campaign' → `jobName`; 'job X' without saying code-vs-name → `job` (ambiguous, matches code OR name). Same pattern for product (`productCode`/`productName`/`product`). **Codes are EXACT (case-sensitive); names are case-insensitive.** **Sample lookup**: `sample` is ambiguous — matches sample UUID OR sampleCode (exact, case-sensitive) OR cfBarcode (exact, case-sensitive) OR sampleName (case-insensitive). Filter by planning session: `session` (ambiguous session UUID, code, or name partial — matches against planningSessionId OR planningSession.sessionCode OR planningSession.sessionName). Drill-down: pass jobIds/productIds/planningSessionIds from upstream queries. Use human-readable names for all filters (resolved to IDs automatically). Returns: current step & status, production type, products, job, samples (codes/names/cfBarcodes/sizes/total/checkedIn), team on set (all 8 roles), vendors, location, style guide, outfit (incl. styling item codes), planning session (id/name/code/start/end), timing. When groupBy params set, returns counts/aggregations instead of list.

- **CF module:** Production
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

<a id="tool-query_editorial_deliverable"></a>
## `query_editorial_deliverable` — Query Editorial Deliverable

Search Editorial Deliverables — the per-output unit inside an Editorial Project (each Deliverable is one delivery row, e.g. 'AEM Deliverable 1', 'D 20230627 3'). Does NOT return sample records — to list or find specific samples, use query_sample. Use to answer: which deliverables exist for a project/campaign, what step a deliverable is at, who owns it, what's overdue, how many at each step, deliverable counts by status/project/workspace/period. Pass deliverableIds to look up specific deliverables by ID (e.g. from detail page context). When any groupBy* param is set, returns aggregation buckets instead of a list. For any 'per workspace' or 'per client' breakdown, use groupByWorkspace=true — do not try to derive workspace names from list results.

Search Editorial Productions (also called Editorial work units) — the central WorkUnit-doc row that tracks an Editorial Deliverable's content through the workflow (contentCreationTypeId=2). Use to answer: which work units exist for a project/deliverable, what step a production is at, who's shooting it, how many at each status/step, throughput by week, work unit counts by project/workspace/photographer. Filter by project (name/code/due-date/custom-property), deliverable (name/code/due-date/custom-property), product code, sample (code/name/custom-property), workflow type ('Asset Workflow' / 'Finalization'), workflow status ('To Do'/'In Progress'/'Done'), current step (Capture/Final Selection/External Post/External Post QC/Internal Post/Internal Post QC/Post Review/Asset Delivery), current step status ('Backlog'/'To Do'/'Rejected'/'In Progress'/'Failed'/'Done'), photographer/videographer/stylist/hair-and-makeup/model/art-director/assistant (Editorial team-on-set), External Post Vendor, External Post QC / Internal Post / Internal Post QC / Post Review assignees, workspace, media type (Image/Video — feature-gated), round of review, asset-delivery-finished date range, Selection/Post-Review collection statuses. When any groupBy* param is set, returns aggregation buckets instead of a list. For any 'per workspace' or 'per client' breakdown, use groupByWorkspace=true — do not try to derive workspace names from list results. Editorial only — for E-comm production rows use query_ecomm_production. For the parent project itself use query_editorial_project; for deliverable-level filtering use query_editorial_deliverable.

<a id="tool-query_planning"></a>
## `query_planning` — Query Planning

**Custom Resource trigger** → if user prompt names a production support role NOT in the standard productionTeam (Photographer/Stylist/Model/Art Director/Hair&Makeup/Assistant/Videographer/DigitalProcessing) → call this tool with `includeCustomResources=true`. Common triggers: 'cater', 'lunch', 'runner', 'driver', 'PA', 'DIT', 'dog handler', 'medic' (and any similar free-form role). Custom Resource labels are FREE-FORM text studios type themselves → semantic-match them yourself from `customResourceLabelsAvailable[]` + `customResources[]` in the response. **Tool-first, ask-later**: call the tool, then if `customResourceLabelsAvailable=[]` ask user; otherwise semantic-match from availableLabels. **Trailing-junk / cut-off tolerance**: if user prompt has trailing backslash (`\`), ellipsis (`...`), question marks (`??`), or appears truncated mid-word, IGNORE the noise and treat the readable trigger word as the query. Do NOT respond with 'your message looks cut off' — call the tool with the cleaned query. Examples: 'Who is today's Cater' → query for cater. 'Lunch...' → query for lunch. 'DIT??' → query for DIT. **Likely-misread tolerance**: if a trigger word could be misread as a proper noun (e.g. 'Cater' → 'Carter', 'DIT' → a person's initials), DEFAULT to the production-role interpretation (this tool is in a production planning context, not a general-knowledge chat). Don't suggest sports/celebrity readings of trigger words. **Default 'today' to ISO date**: when user says 'today', 'hôm nay', 'this morning', etc., automatically set `dateFrom`=`dateTo`=current date in `YYYY-MM-DD` (server timezone UTC). Same for 'tomorrow' (+1 day), 'yesterday' (-1 day), 'this week' (Mon-Sun current week). Don't ask the user to specify the date when they used a relative phrase. Search planning sessions — scheduled production shoots with team, time slots, and progress. Use this to answer: what's planned, when (ISO 8601 UTC), where, who's on set, sample check-in status, photography progress, alerts. **Who-is-working queries**: when user asks 'who is working this week', 'which talent has sessions today', 'list photographers on sessions next month' → set `groupByTeamMember=true` with `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Response flips to person-centric: each entry shows the team member with their sessions. This is the primary way to answer talent-on-session questions when the studio does not use the Resource Booking add-on. Filter by team member (any role) or specific role (photographer, stylist, model, art director, assistant, videographer, hair & makeup). Also filter by sessionCode (e.g. 'SES137123CF'), sessionName (partial), location, production type, check-in/alert/photography status, date range. Filter by associated job (jobCode/jobName, or `job` ambiguous = code OR name) and product attributes (productCode/productName, or `product` ambiguous = code OR name, plus brand, category, color, styleCode) — exact match, case-insensitive, matches if ANY of the session's jobs/products satisfies the filter. Editorial workflow: filter by associated project (projectCode/projectName, or `project` ambiguous = code OR name, plus campaign) and deliverable (deliverableCode/deliverableName, or `deliverable` ambiguous = code OR name, plus deliverableOutputName) — exact match, case-insensitive, matches if ANY of the session's projects/deliverables satisfies the filter. Use `user` to find a session where a given user is on the production team regardless of skill/role (V2 ProductionTeams). Returns: session `id` (UUID), sessionName, sessionCode, time slots (ISO 8601 UTC), full production team (resolved names), check-in status, photography progress, job codes, product codes. When groupBy params set, returns counts/aggregations instead of list. **Session lookup param choice — strict per user phrasing:**   • User says 'session code SES137123CF' / 'code SES…' → `sessionCode` only.   • User says 'session named Nike Spring' / 'the Spring shoot' → `sessionName` only.   • User says 'session SES137123CF' / 'session Nike Spring' WITHOUT specifying code-vs-name → `session` (ambiguous param, matches code OR name OR UUID). Don't pass multiple session params at once — pick the one that matches user intent. **Chain with query_talent_crew_schedule**: when the user asks about bookings/holds for a specific session, FIRST call this tool → take response's `id` and `timeSlots` → pass to `query_talent_crew_schedule(sessionId=&lt;id>, dateFrom=&lt;min start>, dateTo=&lt;max end>, ...)`. **Custom Resource queries** (cater / catering / lunch / food / runner / driver / transport / PA / production assistant / makeup artist (one-off) / any role NOT in standard productionTeam): set `includeCustomResources=true`. Custom resources are free-form (label, name) pairs attached inline to a session via the FE 'CUSTOM RESOURCE' panel → free-form means studios type whatever they want ('cater', 'Cater', 'catering', 'lunch', 'food service'). The tool returns ALL custom resources on the page and Claude does the semantic match (no server-side filter — too many false-negatives on free-form text like 'Caster' vs 'cater'). **Semantic match rule** (CRITICAL for custom resources): the response includes `customResourceLabelsAvailable: string[]` → distinct labels seen on the page, plus `customResources[{label,name}]` per session. Scan `customResourceLabelsAvailable` for labels **semantically similar** to the user's word, then read the matching `customResources` entries. DO NOT reply 'not found' until you've checked every label. Examples: 'cater' → look for 'catering', 'lunch', 'meal', 'food service', 'snack runner'; 'driver' → 'transport', 'shuttle', 'logistics'; 'PA' → 'production assistant', 'runner', 'gopher'. Tell the user which labels you considered (e.g. 'No exact 'cater' label, but 'catering' is set to John Smith → likely the same role.'). **Custom resource has NO booking status** (no Confirmed/Hold) → it's session-inline data, not a resource booking. Don't mention status pills for these rows.

<a id="tool-query_talent_crew"></a>
## `query_talent_crew` — Query Talent & Crew

Search talent and resource users — both license users (internal team members) and resource users (freelancers, models, agencies). Use this to answer: who is on the team, who has a given skill, what agency a model belongs to, counts of talent by skill / employment type / status. User types: License (internal), Resource (external). Employment types: Permanent, Freelance. States: Enabled, Disabled, NotVerify, Deleted. Common skills: Photographer, Stylist, Model, Art Director, Hair & Makeup, Retoucher, Videographer, Producer, Assistant, Project Manager, Deliverable Owner, Digital Processing. Filter by name, job title, user type, employment type, skill, state, agency, short list, contact info, city, created date range. Pass `talentCrewIds` (JSON array of talent crew IDs from query_talent_crew_schedule or other tools) to look up specific records directly instead of re-querying by skill. Use human-readable names for all filters (resolved to IDs automatically). Each record includes a `deepLinkUrl` to the talent detail page in the web app. **CRITICAL — UI rendering ownership**: an inline widget handles record-list and aggregation responses, so your text must NOT duplicate them. Per response shape:   • `hits` with ≥1 talent → widget renders compact-card / table. Text = ONE brief sentence (e.g. 'Found 6 talents in the Christmas 24 short list.').   • Aggregation (`byAgency` / `bySkill` / `byStatus` / `byUserType` / `byEmploymentType`) → widget renders bar-chart sections. Text = ONE brief sentence summarising top buckets (e.g. '15 agencies, top 3: ACME (12), aaa (9), 234234 (8).').   • `hits` empty + `total > 0` (count-only, pageSize=0) → widget HIDES (0 height). Text MUST state the count plainly (e.g. 'Có **123** photographers đang active.').   • `hits` empty + `total = 0` → widget HIDES. Text = brief negative reply (e.g. 'Không có crew member nào match.'). Do NOT write a markdown table, list, gallery, or any field-by-field summary. Do NOT embed `!\[image](avatarUrl)` or `[Show Image](url)`. Do NOT include deep-link URLs in text — the widget already renders the name as a clickable anchor. Avatars are shown by default in compact-card and table views. Pass `includeAvatar=false` only when the caller explicitly wants to skip avatar resolution (e.g. perf-sensitive bulk queries). Still no markdown images in your text — the widget owns the visual. **"Talent" terminology** — `skill="Talent"` is a PSEUDO-SKILL meaning Models + AI Models only (server-side OR-match). ✅ TRIGGER on standalone words: "talent", "talents", "a talent", "the talents", "find a talent", "show me talents", "model agency", or context implying Models specifically. Examples: 'Find a talent named Jane' → { name: 'Jane', skill: 'Talent' }; 'How many talents do we have?' → { skill: 'Talent', pageSize: 0 }. ❌ DO NOT TRIGGER on: 'Talent & Crew' / 'Talent and Crew' / 'talents and crew' — these are the FULL ENTITY NAME (License + Resource = whole pool). They contain the word "Talent" but mean the OPPOSITE — search broad pool, omit `skill`. Examples: 'Find Talent & Crew named Han' → { name: 'Han' } NO skill; 'How many Talent & Crew based in London' → { city: 'London' } NO skill. ❌ DO NOT TRIGGER for explicit roles (Photographers, Stylists, Producers, Hair & Makeup, Videographers, internal team) — pass the explicit skill name or omit the filter. When groupBy params are set, returns counts / aggregations instead of a list. Each hit includes a `rates` array (rateId, name, amount, currency, duration, rateType, agencyFee, payrollFee, isDefault, description) **only if the caller has the `Rates` screen permission**. Top-level `ratesAccess` is `granted` when rates are emitted and `denied` when they are gated out — when `denied`, do not assume the talent has no rates configured, the field is simply hidden by permission. **Rates are sensitive financial data — the widget HIDES them by default.** Even when `ratesAccess=granted` and the `rates` array is populated, the widget does NOT render the rates block in any view (compact card, table drill-down) unless `columns` explicitly includes 'rates'. The schedule tool widget never renders rates. This is a data-minimization safeguard against accidental leaks during screen-shares and casual lookups. To surface rates in the widget, set `columns: ['rates']` (or include 'rates' alongside other columns). You can still reason about rates in your text reply — but only when the user explicitly asked. **STRICT RULE for the `columns` parameter** — you MUST set it whenever the user names specific fields or uses narrowing words ('just', 'only', 'only show', 'just show', 'chỉ', 'chỉ hiển thị', 'khÃ´ng cần'). Do NOT fall back to defaults in those cases. Mapping examples:  • 'List 10 photographers and **just** show their skills' → call with arguments: { skill: 'Photographer', pageSize: 10, columns: ['skills'] }   • '5 models with their **rate info only**' → { skill: 'Model', pageSize: 5, columns: ['rates'] }   • '**Emails and phones** of all stylists' → { skill: 'Stylist', columns: ['email','phone'] }   • 'Which agency does each model belong to' → { skill: 'Model', columns: ['agencies'] }   • 'Talent based in London' → { city: 'London' }   • 'Talent in the Fashion Crew short list' → { shortListName: 'Fashion Crew' }   • 'Talent who are both Photographer AND Videographer' → { skill: 'Photographer|Videographer' }   • 'NotVerify accounts older than 30 days' → { state: 'NotVerify', createdTo: '&lt;today-30d ISO>' }   • 'How many new talents joined in the last 3 months' → { createdFrom: '&lt;today-3m ISO>', pageSize: 0 } (read total)   • 'List talents grouped by skill' (aggregation) → omit columns; the param has no effect on aggregation mode.   • Generic 'list/show me photographers' (no narrowing word) → omit columns; defaults to a broad set. Photo and Name are always rendered as anchors regardless of `columns`. Available column ids: jobTitle, type, employment, status, skills, agencies, email, phone, location, createdAt, pronouns, userCode, rates.

**MANDATORY TRIGGERS** — when user prompt contains ANY of: 'available', 'availability', 'schedule', 'booking', 'confirmed', 'on hold', '1st hold', '2nd hold', 'next week', 'this week', 'on May/June/...', 'free on', 'busy on', 'OOO', 'out of office', 'unavailable on', 'inactive', 'haven't been booked', 'not booked in N days', 'access cleanup', 'dormant', 'idle freelancers' → you MUST call this tool. Do NOT respond with markdown tables, lists, or hallucinate data. The widget will render the answer visually. **Inverse query** (find talents WITHOUT bookings) → use `onlyInactive=true` paired with `dateFrom/dateTo` for the inactivity window. Common phrasings: 'freelancers not booked in 60+ days' → `onlyInactive=true, dateFrom=&lt;60d ago>, dateTo=&lt;today>` (chain with `query_talent_crew(employmentType=Freelancer, view=data)` first to scope pool to freelancers). **NEGATIVE TRIGGER — route to `query_planning` instead** when the prompt names a free-form production SUPPORT role like cater, catering, lunch, food, runner, driver, PA, DIT, dog handler, medic, security, prop master, set decorator, etc. These are NOT skills (skills = Photographer/Stylist/Model/Art Director/Hair&Makeup/Assistant/Videographer/DigitalProcessing). They are Custom Resource labels attached inline to planning sessions. **Do NOT pass them as `skill=...` here → the master skill catalog will not match them and the tool will return 0**. Use `query_planning(includeCustomResources=true)` instead. Query Talent & Crew scheduling data from the Resourcing Calendar — User Availability (Available/OutOfOffice/Unavailable set by the user) and Resource Bookings (1stHold/2ndHold/Confirmed/Unavailable set by manager). Use for: who is available next week, who is confirmed for a shoot date, stale holds, overbooking conflicts, per-record schedule, capacity overview. **This tool ALSO serves as a list view of talents matching the skill filter** — do NOT pre-call query_talent_crew when user prompt combines list+schedule intent (e.g. 'list all Models then their schedule next week'). Pass `skill` directly here for both the list and the schedule in ONE call. **Chain mode**: when the result is being passed as input to another tool (intermediate data extraction, NOT user-facing), set `view=data` to suppress widget render and skip avatar resolution (saves ~150ms). Default `view=widget` is correct for ALL user-facing answers. Requires dateFrom + dateTo. Scope is OPTIONAL. **Do NOT chain via query_talent_crew to pre-resolve IDs by skill.** Pass `skill` directly here — the tool resolves talents internally. When you also pass `availabilityStatus` or `bookingStatus`, the tool runs **status-first**: scans the whole studio crew pool (cap 500), filters by status, then post-filters by skill — this catches talents that a skill-first scope (cap 50) would miss. Use cases for unscoped queries: 'how many crew are unavailable on May 8?' (set pageSize=0 for count-only), 'who is Out of Office next week?'. **Name-scoped queries — mandatory chain.** When the user names a SPECIFIC talent (proper name: 'AloHa NN', 'John Photographer', 'show schedule for Tien'): FIRST call `query_talent_crew(name=..., view=data)` to resolve name → ID(s), then pass those as `talentCrewIds` here. Do NOT call this tool unscoped expecting to find the named talent in the result list — that wastes a round trip and dumps the whole crew on the user. **Session-scoped queries — chain order is mandatory.** When the user mentions a session: FIRST call `query_planning` to resolve the session — pick the right session param: `sessionCode` if user said it's a code, `sessionName` if a name, `session` if ambiguous. Then use the response's `id` (UUID) as `sessionId` here, and `timeSlots` to derive `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Do NOT call this tool first with a raw code/name — it requires a UUID. **Do NOT drop `sessionId` as a fallback** when a session-scoped query returns 0. Zero IS the answer — it means the session has no records matching the filters. Report 0 to the user (e.g. 'no 1st/2nd Hold bookings for that session — the crew are Confirmed instead'). To find out what status the session crew DO have, drop the `bookingStatus` filter while keeping `sessionId` — never the other way around. For session team composition ('who is on session X') use query_planning instead. sessionId here filters bookings linked to a specific session (1st Hold / Confirmed per shoot). Availability statuses (User Availability set by the user): Available, OutOfOffice, Unavailable. Booking statuses (Resource Booking set by manager): typically Option, Contacted, Confirmed, 1st Hold (FirstHold), 2nd Hold (SecondHold), Released, Cancelled, Unavailable — exact list depends on studio config (see _debug.cachedBookingStatusNames). Pass the canonical name (case-insensitive) — server resolves to dynamic statusId. **Multi-status filter — `bookingStatuses` / `availabilityStatuses`**: pass a JSON array of names (e.g. `bookingStatuses=["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"]`) when the intent covers multiple statuses. Records matching ANY listed status pass. Use the plural form whenever the user phrasing implies a set, not a single canonical status. **Singular vs multi → decide by user word, not by intent**. RULE: if user prompt contains an explicit canonical status word ('confirmed', '1st hold', 'first hold', '2nd hold', 'second hold', 'option', 'contacted', 'released', 'cancelled') → use SINGULAR `bookingStatus=&lt;that word>`. Examples: 'who is **confirmed** today' → `bookingStatus=Confirmed`. 'show me **1st holds** for May 14' → `bookingStatus=FirstHold`. 'anyone **on hold** today' (vague — 1st or 2nd) → `bookingStatuses=["FirstHold","SecondHold"]`. Only use the multi-status form when the user prompt is VAGUE about status: 'who is **working/on-floor/on the books/scheduled/booked** today' → active bookings → `bookingStatuses=["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"]`. **Heuristic**: if the user typed a status word verbatim, that's the filter → singular. If they typed a generic 'working/scheduled' verb, multi. Don't mix. **Booking-vs-Availability AND-gate (LH-50337 follow-up)**: when ANY booking-status filter is set, the tool now narrows availability records to talents that survived the booking filter (and vice versa). So `bookingStatuses=[...]` will NOT leak availability-only rows for talents without a matching booking. Translation: filtering 'Confirmed today' returns only talents who actually have a Confirmed booking on that day, even though their availability records overlap. When groupBy params set, returns bucket counts instead of list. **Rendering rule**: each record carries a `deepLinkUrl`. When presenting results in text, ALWAYS wrap `displayName` as a clickable markdown link: `[displayName](deepLinkUrl)`. Never print plain names. If `displayName` is empty, fall back to talentCrewId or userCode (still wrapped). **UI rendering**: paired widget renders avatar table with status pills + inline date ranges + clickable names (Availability / Booking / On-set Role columns auto-shown when relevant data present). Per response shape:   • `hits` with ≥1 talent → widget renders compact-card / table. Text = ONE brief sentence summary PLUS optionally ONE useful insight you spot in the data (e.g. 'Found 6 confirmed photographers for May 8 — note: oanh eu has overlapping bookings May 7-15.'). Do not list each row in text — widget shows the data.   • Aggregation (`byAvailabilityStatus` / `byBookingStatus`) → widget renders bar chart. Text = ONE brief sentence summarising buckets.   • `hits` empty + `total > 0` (count-only, pageSize=0) → widget HIDES. Text MUST state the count plainly.   • `hits` empty + `total = 0` → widget HIDES. **IMPORTANT fallback**: before replying 'no one is booked', call `query_planning(dateFrom=&lt;same>, dateTo=&lt;same>, groupByTeamMember=true)` to check if talent are assigned on sessions without bookings. If `query_planning` returns teamMembers, present those results to the user (e.g. 'No bookings found, but these talent are assigned on sessions this week:'). Only reply 'no one is planned' if BOTH tools return empty. **Conflict API unavailability**: if `_debug.conflictApiAvailable === false`, the booking conflict service is down for this query. ALL hits will have `hasConflict=false` regardless of actual state. The widget renders a footer note, but you SHOULD also append a brief warning to your text reply (e.g. 'Note: conflict warnings are temporarily unavailable — verify holds manually'). **INACTIVE BOOKINGS — STRICT RULE**: by default the tool excludes `Cancelled` and `Released` bookings from results (active-schedule hygiene). If `_debug.inactiveCount.total > 0` in the response, the widget rendered fewer rows than exist server-side. Mention this in the text reply (e.g. 'X cancelled / Y released bookings hidden — let me know if you want to see them.'). Pass `includeInactiveBookings=true` ONLY when the user EXPLICITLY mentions cancelled, released, inactive, or 'all bookings' (e.g. 'show all bookings including cancelled', 'were any of Tien's holds released?'). Do NOT pass it for generic 'schedule for X' or 'who's available' queries. **Rates are NEVER shown via this tool.** Schedule queries are about availability and bookings, not pricing. The widget for this tool does not render rates in any view (single, list, or drill-down). If the user asks about rates after a schedule query, chain to `query_talent_crew(talentCrewIds=[&lt;from schedule result>], columns=['rates'])` instead of re-calling the schedule tool. Do NOT write a markdown table, do NOT chain to get_talent_crew_preview, do NOT fabricate avatar URLs in text. Do NOT include deep-link URLs in text — the widget renders the name as a clickable anchor.

- **CF module:** Resourcing Calendar
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

<details>
<summary>Show all 18 parameters</summary>

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `talentCrewIds` | JsonElement? | no | Talent crew IDs (JSON array) from query_talent_crew. E.g. ["id1","id2"]. Max 50. |
| `talentCrewId` | string | no | Single talent crew ID — for per-record schedule view. |
| `skill` | string | no | Skill name to scope talent pool e.g. Photographer. Resolved via talentcrew ES. Max 50 results. |
| `dateFrom` | string | no | Start date ISO e.g. 2026-06-01 (required). |
| `dateTo` | string | no | End date ISO e.g. 2026-06-07 (required). |
| `availabilityStatus` | string | no | Filter User Availability status: Available, OutOfOffice, Unavailable. |
| `availabilityStatuses` | JsonElement? | no | Multi-status User Availability filter — JSON array of canonical names, e.g. ["Available","OutOfOffice"]. Records matching ANY listed status pass. Takes precedence over `availabilityStatus` when both supplied. |
| `bookingStatus` | string | no | Filter Resource Booking status — case-insensitive. Common values: Option, Contacted, Confirmed, FirstHold (or '1st Hold'), SecondHold (or '2nd Hold'), Released, Cancelled, Unavailable. Studio-specific list available in _debug.cachedBookingStatusNames. NOTE: by default Cancelled and Released are hidden (data hygiene); pass them explicitly here to see only those, or pass `includeInactiveBookings=true` to see them alongside active bookings. |
| `bookingStatuses` | JsonElement? | no | Multi-status Resource Booking filter — JSON array of canonical names, e.g. ["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"] for active bookings. Records matching ANY listed status pass. Takes precedence over `bookingStatus` when both supplied. **Recommended over `bookingStatus` for 'who is working today / on-floor / scheduled' queries** — pass ["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"] to capture all real holds in one call instead of inferring `Confirmed` only. |
| `includeInactiveBookings` | bool | no | Include Cancelled and Released bookings in results. Default false (these statuses clutter the active-schedule view). Pass true ONLY when user EXPLICITLY mentions cancelled, released, inactive, or 'all bookings'. If `bookingStatus` is set explicitly (e.g. to 'Cancelled'), that takes precedence and this flag becomes irrelevant. |
| `onlyInactive` | bool | no | **Inverse mode** — return ONLY talents in the pool that have ZERO bookings overlapping [dateFrom..dateTo]. Use for 'who hasn't been booked recently' / 'inactive freelancers' / 'access cleanup' queries (e.g. 'which freelancers haven't been booked in 60+ days'). The pool is determined by the usual sources (talentCrewIds, sessionId, or the full studio crew). When set, the tool clears all booking/availability records before rendering, forces phantom emission, and bypasses status filters (bookingStatus*/availabilityStatus* become noise). Pair with `dateFrom=&lt;60d ago>, dateTo=&lt;today>` for the canonical use case. Skill / employmentType narrowing: chain via `query_talent_crew(employmentType=Freelancer, view=data)` first to get IDs, then pass as `talentCrewIds` here. Default false — normal mode returns talents WITH records. |
| `sessionId` | string | no | Filter bookings linked to a specific session — must be the session UUID. If the user gave a session code, name, or ambiguous identifier, you MUST first call `query_planning` (use `sessionCode` for explicit codes, `sessionName` for explicit names, `session` for ambiguous) to resolve it; pass the returned `id` here, and use `timeSlots` to set dateFrom + dateTo. Passing a non-UUID returns an error. |
| `bookingCreatedBefore` | string | no | ISO date — return only bookings created before this date (surface stale holds). |
| `groupByAvailabilityStatus` | bool | no | Aggregation: group by User Availability status and return counts. |
| `groupByBookingStatus` | bool | no | Aggregation: group by Resource Booking status and return counts. |
| `hasConflict` | bool | no | Health: return only talents with active overbooking conflicts (conflictStatusId 105/106/107). |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Max results in list mode (ignored in aggregation). Set to 0 for COUNT-only mode — response keeps `totalAvailabilities` + `totalBookings` (full counts after status/session filtering) but omits the item arrays. Use this when the user asks 'how many ...' without needing per-record details. |
| `view` | string | no | View mode: `widget` (default) renders the avatar table widget; `data` returns the same records under `data[]` with `hits=[]` (widget auto-hides) and SKIPS avatar resolution. **Use `view=data` ONLY when the result is being chained as input to another tool call (intermediate data extraction)**, NOT for user-facing answers. Example chain: extract talent IDs to feed into a follow-up query_asset(talentCrewId=...) call. Default `widget` is correct for ALL user-facing answers. |

</details>

**Example input**

```json
{ "dateFrom": "2026-06-10", "dateTo": "2026-06-20", "bookingStatus": "Confirmed", "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 5, "hits": [ { "talentCrewId": "t-101", "displayName": "Jane Doe", "availabilityStatus": "Available", "bookingStatus": "Confirmed", "onSetRole": "Photographer", "hasConflict": false } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

Availability + bookings grouped by talent. Status is filtered in-memory (the planning backend has no status filter); skill is applied as a post-filter.

<a id="tool-query_task"></a>
## `query_task` — Query Task

Search tasks (individual workflow steps). Status: New, Todo, InProgress, Rejected, QCRejected, Failed, Bypassed, Done. Use names for step, production type, assignee, vendor, workspace. Can filter by product/job/workspace and includes product, job, assignee info in results. When groupBy params set, returns counts/aggregations instead of list. For any 'per workspace' or 'per client' breakdown, use groupByWorkspace=true.

- **CF module:** Workflow
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

<details>
<summary>Show all 25 parameters</summary>

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `taskId` | string | no | Task ID (exact match) |
| `status` | string | no | Step status name |
| `step` | string | no | Step name: Photography, InternalPostProduction, FinalSelection, etc. |
| `productionType` | string | no | Production type name or ID |
| `assignee` | string | no | Assignee name or user ID |
| `postProductionVendor` | string | no | Post-production vendor name or ID |
| `jobCode` | string | no | Job code |
| `jobName` | string | no | Job name |
| `productCode` | string | no | Product code (exact) |
| `productName` | string | no | Product name (exact) |
| `product` | string | no | Search product by code or name (OR) |
| `dateFrom` | string | no | Finished date from (ISO) |
| `dateTo` | string | no | Finished date to (ISO) |
| `workspace` | string | no | Workspace/client name or ID |
| `startedFrom` | string | no | Started date from (ISO) |
| `startedTo` | string | no | Started date to (ISO) |
| `groupByStep` | bool | no | Group by step — aggregation mode |
| `groupByStatus` | bool | no | Group by status — aggregation mode |
| `groupByAssignee` | bool | no | Group by assignee — aggregation mode |
| `groupByVendor` | bool | no | Group by vendor — aggregation mode |
| `groupByProductionType` | bool | no | Group by production type — aggregation mode |
| `groupByPeriod` | string | no | Group by period: hour, day, week, month — aggregation mode |
| `groupByWorkspace` | bool | no | Group by workspace/client — aggregation mode. Use for any 'per workspace', 'per client', 'by workspace' question. |
| `pageSize` | int | no | Max results (ignored in aggregation) |
| `page` | int | no | Page (0-based, ignored in aggregation) |

</details>

**Example input**

```json
{ "status": "InProgress", "step": "InternalPostProduction", "assignee": "John Smith", "pageSize": 10 }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 11, "hits": [ { "taskId": "wk1...", "step": "InternalPostProduction", "status": "InProgress", "assignee": "John Smith" } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

One workflow step per row. Status values: New, Todo, InProgress, Rejected, QCRejected, Failed, Bypassed, Done.

<a id="tool-query_workspace"></a>
## `query_workspace` — Query Workspace

List workspaces (clients) in the studio with their calendar & timezone settings. Returns: id, name, isDefault, isEnabled, timezoneDisplayName, startDayOfWeek, firstWeekOfYear. **Use cases**: (1) Enumerate workspace names/IDs before grouping or filtering other entities by workspace. (2) Get a workspace's timezone and calendar settings. Pass 'keyword' for server-side partial name search; omit to get all workspaces. Use workspace IDs from the result to pass as 'workspace' filter to other query tools (query_ecomm_production, query_ecomm_job, query_ecomm_product_request, etc.).

- **CF module:** Workspaces
- **Read-only:** yes · **Idempotent:** yes · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `keyword` | string | no | Search workspace by name (partial match, case-insensitive). Omit to list all. |

**Example input**

```json
{ "keyword": "acme" }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "total": 2, "hits": [ { "id": "8a...", "name": "Acme Studio", "isDefault": true, "isEnabled": true, "timezoneDisplayName": "Europe/London", "startDayOfWeek": "Monday" } ] }
```

**Known limitations**

Returns workspace/client configuration only. Use the returned `id`s as the `workspace` filter on the other query tools.

<a id="tool-send_feedback"></a>
## `send_feedback` — Send Feedback

Send feedback to the Creative Force team. Types: result_feedback (rate a result), unsolved_question (couldn't get an answer), feature_request (want new capability).

- **CF module:** Platform
- **Read-only:** no · **Idempotent:** no · **Destructive:** no

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|:--------:|-------------|
| `type` | string | **yes** | Feedback type: result_feedback, unsolved_question, or feature_request |
| `message` | string | **yes** | Your comment, question, or request |
| `rating` | string | no | Rating (for result_feedback): correct, incorrect, or partial |
| `relatedToolName` | string | no | Which tool produced the result |
| `relatedToolInput` | string | no | Parameters used in the related tool call |
| `relatedToolOutput` | string | no | Summary of what the tool returned |

**Example input**

```json
{ "type": "result_feedback", "rating": "correct", "message": "Job list was accurate", "relatedToolName": "query_ecomm_job" }
```

**Example output**

```json
{ "status": "received", "type": "result_feedback" }
```

**Known limitations**

The only write tool (not read-only). Persistence to a database is not yet implemented; feedback is logged and forwarded to Slack (best-effort).
